title: Engine-aware collation, ENUM, and text-width governance with dedicated runtime persistence wiring

phases.objective: Block unsupported or conflicting database collations, enum seed literals, text-width overflows, and ordered schema/view dependency gaps before migration apply, while preserving governed response chunk persistence through an independently configured runtime persistence pool.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Governed migration preflight and governed tool response chunk persistence
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Supported collation DDL passes policy, unsupported or implicit DDL is blocked, and chunk persistence fails closed without dedicated runtime persistence configuration.
steps: Detect the active database engine through the governed pool.
Evaluate migration DDL against the engine-aware charset and collation policy.
For a first push whose CI event carries an all-zero before SHA, omit that invalid diff base and evaluate the parent of the exact head instead.

When a syntactically valid base SHA is unavailable after a force-push or non-ancestor update, retry the collation diff against the exact head parent rather than failing open or blocking unrelated work.
Reject unknown engines, implicit defaults, or mixed join-key collations before apply.
Project MariaDB ENUM domains across the complete ordered migration chain and reject unsupported INSERT, REPLACE, or UPDATE literals before apply.
Project MariaDB bounded text widths across the complete ordered migration chain and reject literal INSERT, REPLACE, or UPDATE overflow before apply.
Evaluate static CONCAT and CONCAT_WS append expressions against the projected bounded text domain, including direct and COALESCE/IFNULL/NULLIF-wrapped target columns.
Evaluate qualified columns used by ordered CREATE VIEW statements against the schema state available before each view, while treating derived views and system schemas conservatively.
Evaluate every explicit INSERT column list against its VALUES tuple(s) or SELECT projection, including nested expressions and quoted literals, before disposable schema apply.
Apply platform_runtime_config.note and execution_policies scope-column TEXT alignment before the first ordered descriptive writer.
Resolve the dedicated runtime persistence pool for governed response chunks.
Verify least-privilege readiness and same-source chunk readback or fail closed when configuration is absent.
assertions: Unknown or undetected database engines never reach migration apply.
MariaDB/MySQL new-table DDL requires explicit utf8mb4 and policy-approved collation.
An all-zero CI before SHA never reaches git diff as a base revision; the collation guard falls back to the exact head parent.
An unavailable but syntactically valid CI base SHA fails closed only if the exact head-parent fallback also fails; otherwise the collation guard evaluates that bounded parent diff.
Runtime persistence uses RUNTIME_PERSISTENCE_DB_* identity rather than DB_USER fallback.
Missing dedicated runtime persistence configuration returns a bounded 503 and no durable mutation.
ENUM-domain/seed mismatches fail closed before Docker or any database connection.
Text-width/literal and static append-expression overflow mismatches fail closed before Docker or any database connection.
The platform runtime note and execution-policy scope domains are unbounded before their ordered writers; no later writer may rely on the historical VARCHAR(255) width.
A qualified column referenced by an ordered view must exist on its base table before CREATE VIEW; missing columns fail closed before Docker or any database connection.
INSERT column/value arity mismatches fail closed before Docker or any database connection; policy seeds for execution_policies must provide all eight declared values.
Every schema object exposed to the Work Map coverage matrix is classified by the canonical registry before generated Work Map writing; unresolved objects remain fail-closed.

phases.objective: Provision and read back separate Hostinger runtime persistence identity and grants after explicit infrastructure approval.
Add runtime persistence outage recovery and collation drift reconciliation evidence.
Exercise one non-production tenant with the dedicated runtime persistence identity and governed collation readback.
Verify production grants and schema readback only after approved Hostinger provisioning and redeployment.
